articles.title: 🔍 A.I. Search Startup's Value Balloons Past A Small Nation's Budget; Now Too Big To Actually Answer Your Question
articles.dateline: SILICON VALLEY — reported after a very long 'thinking…' spinner
paras: An AI search company's valuation reportedly leapt from around $20 billion last year toward the stratosphere, with revenue topping $750 million as it pushes beyond mere search into "agents" that handle complex professional tasks — meaning it has graduated from answering your questions to confidently doing your job.

"We're redefining how people find information," the company said, of a service now worth more than several countries and most human feelings. Analysts note the thesis is simple: if you own the box everyone types their questions into, you can eventually charge for the answers, the follow-ups, and possibly the silence in between.

articles.title: 🚸 New Zealand Moves To Ban Kids From The Apps; Teens Discover The Ancient Art Of Lying About Their Birthday
articles.dateline: WELLINGTON — reported past a suspiciously tall 12-year-old
paras: New Zealand advanced legislation to keep young users off certain platforms, joining a global wave of age-ban laws — a well-meaning effort destined to be defeated, as always, within minutes, by a teenager and a birth year ending in a suspiciously round number.

"We're protecting young people," lawmakers said, of rules that assume the internet can reliably tell how old anyone is, a thing it has never once managed to do. Experts note that the timeless teenage skill of clicking "yes, I am 40 years old" remains humanity's most durable and completely undefeated technology.

articles.title: 📱 Folding Phones Now Fold So Much They're Basically Origami; One More Crease And It's A Paper Crane
articles.dateline: SEOUL — reported along yet another hinge
paras: The latest wave of folding-phone breakthroughs has devices bending thinner, flatter, and more times than ever — a relentless march that will end, logically, with a smartphone you fold into a swan and place gently on the mantel.

"It's the future of form factors," makers insist, of phones that now fold in half, then in half again, chasing a horizon where the device is technically a pamphlet. Reviewers admire the engineering while noting that the more a phone folds, the more ways it has learned to develop a mysterious crease exactly where you look most.

articles.title: 💰 Chip Giant Warns Customers Of Price Hikes; The Toll Booth On The A.I. Highway Raises Its Rates Again
articles.dateline: SANTA CLARA — filed while re-reading the invoice
paras: The dominant AI chipmaker reportedly warned customers to brace for price increases, gently reminding the entire industry that the road to artificial intelligence runs through exactly one toll booth — and the toll booth has noticed.

"Costs reflect demand," the company explained, to buyers with no realistic alternative and a deepening familiarity with the phrase "take it or leave it." Analysts note that when everyone needs your product to compete, "the price went up" is less a business update and more a weather forecast.

articles.title: 🐌 New A.I. Models Deliberately Think Slower To Be Smarter; Finally, A Computer That Says 'Let Me Get Back To You'
articles.dateline: THE DATA CENTER — reported during a long, thoughtful pause
paras: The latest frontier models increasingly trade raw speed for accuracy, taking extra time to "reason" before answering — meaning that, after decades of demanding faster computers, we have finally built one that thoughtfully asks for a minute.

"Slower is smarter," researchers explained, of models that now pause, ponder, and double-check like a wise elder instead of blurting out the first thing that comes to mind. Users report the answers are markedly better and the waiting markedly worse, proving once again you cannot have everything — even from a machine that cost a billion dollars.

horoscopes.text: An A.I. will take its sweet time answering you today. Breathe. Genius, apparently, now buffers.
You will be asked to prove your age online. Mercury suggests honesty; recorded history suggests otherwise.
Mercury folds a phone into a crane. Beauty is fragile, expensive, and creased exactly where you look.

tech_tip: If an A.I. takes longer to answer now, that's a feature — it's 'thinking.' If YOU take longer, that's a meeting. Life remains deeply unfair.
gadget_watch: Folding phones keep folding toward full origami, chip prices keep climbing, and your new A.I. would like a moment to think, thank you. The future: slower, pricier, and available in swan.
